title: The Healing of the Paralytic and Christ's Authority
english: He does not boast loudly, nor does he proclaim himself before the miracles. He says: 'I wish to, but I have no man'; for where there is no friend, there is no man anywhere.

Because of this I ask, not so that I might learn—for who does not desire to make the weak healthy?—but so that you may show the coarseness of your useful citizens, that they did not give you a hand to throw you into the spring, which even an enemy, if asked, would have provided. Since until now you had no man to throw you into the pool, behold, he who became a man through you and without waters, I heal your passion: 'Arise, take up your bed and go' (John 5:8).

He does not command him to carry the bed simply; for what he did regarding the loaves, he does also here. Just as there he commands the leavings of the loaves to be carried, so here, to make the miracle great and to free the healing from Jewish suspicion and to show that he is not a deceiver, but a savior and a physician common to nature, he commands him to carry the bed.

So the Jews said: 'It is a Sabbath; it is not permitted for you to carry the bed.' But he answers: 'He who made me healthy, that one said to me: Take up your bed and walk' (John 5:8). So they said to him: 'And who is he?' But the healed man did not know. As soon as we learned that it is Jesus who made him healthy, they pursued him in order to kill him.

What then is the Christ? He brings the Father by saying: 'My Father is working until now, and I am working' (John 5:17). For just as, he says, my Father does not submit to mountains, does not serve laws, nor waits for commands, but does with a domestic will what he wills, so I also work all things with authentic authority, equal to the Father.

Because of this they sought even more to kill him, because not only did he loose the Sabbath, but he also called his own Father God, making himself equal to God. But while they were being released and raging, what is the Christ? 'Amen I say to you, the Son cannot do anything of himself unless he sees the Father doing; for whatever he does, the Son likewise does' (John 5:19).

Not because he himself creates other things and I work other things by imitation; for if it were so, there would have to be two heavens, two suns, two seas, two kinds of men and a double cosmos, the one of the Father and mine. For just as lines are set before painters and elements before teachers, so the creation of the Father is set forth, of which I worked by imitation. If it is not so, Lord, why do you say...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG In illud Non potest u01-rem-early

title: The Unity of Action and Will
english: Can the Son do anything of his own accord, unless he sees the Father doing it? I say this to overturn the madness of the Jews who think I am acting lawlessly toward the Father; for since they accuse me concerning the loosening of the Sabbath, I said that 'My Father has been working until now, and I am working' (John 5:17), in order to show the equality on both sides. But all the foolish ones, having supposed that I was setting work against work and opposing opinion to opinion, began to move toward envy; therefore, correcting their opinion, I said: 'The Son cannot do anything of his own accord, unless he looks toward the Father doing it.' Why do you thoughtless ones of the Sabbath harass and examine me, saying that I loose the Sabbath? But I do not oppose the Father, for it is not he who wants to set the Sabbath [in a certain way] and I to loose it; I do not fight against him, I do not stage a rebellion against the opinion; it is not he who wants [one thing] and I want something else; what he wants, I want; what he wills, I will; what he does, I do.

For in this way I do nothing outside of him, nor do I will, because I say something that makes the matter impossible: Amen, I say, the Son cannot do anything of his own accord; for I do not have a will separated and severed from the Father. For since the nature is one and the will is one, it is necessary that the result be one. Therefore the Son cannot do anything of his own accord, for he cannot do anything without the Father, having the whole of him within himself; for I am in the Father and the Father in me. If indeed the works of soul and body are indistinguishable because of their union, even though the nature is divided—one being a mortal body and the other an immortal soul—how can the works of me and of the Father be distinguished? Where will, and word, and knowledge, and wisdom, and nature, and deity are one, the Son cannot do anything of his own accord because of not being separated from the Father, unless he sees the Father doing it, that is, unless he sees not wanting the Father.

For as having the will as a companion of the same very nature, it brings about the things that come to be; for if they complete the work in a bodily way, it is necessary that the construction of the happening be shared. And since a will is sufficient for the bringing forth of non-beings, for this reason also the creation of all things, I know the Father and the Son to be creators not driven out by the Spirit. For whatever he, the Father, does, the Son likewise does; these are the same things and not different things, for not by imitation are others [done].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Son's Unity with the Father in Word and Work
english: I do not [act alone], but I perform the same works that the Father performs. Therefore, having placed my words upon Him, I said: The words which I speak to you I do not speak from myself, but the Father who remains in me performs the works (John 5:37). To Him I have dedicated the works and the words, not to show that I fulfill a service, but to show that I am thus united to the Father by nature, as to have neither word nor work without Him.

Therefore I said, coming: Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me (John 10:38); and if not, believe even through the works. Just as I was saying there that the Father who remains in me performs the works, so also I say here that the works which He performs, these the Son also performs similarly; these and not such [others].

Therefore, 'The Son cannot do anything of himself; will He not at all restore to me my freedom?' Understand; for whatever I wish to do, I am able to do from myself, but I do not wish to. For if the Father loves the Son and shows Him all that He Himself does, how could I hide the One doing all through me? He performs through me, not as through a subordinate; for I am not a subordinate but I work in cooperation, not fulfilling a service but possessing authority. For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, having the power in conjunction with His will, so also I do not raise the dead by fulfilling a service, but by power, authority, right, and will, because I am the one who raises and judges those whom I raise.

For the Father judges no one; but not because of weakness does He not judge, but because He has given all judgment to the Son; for through whom He worked, through him also He judges. Because of this He does all things, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father (John 5:23). For He perceives honor most when He sees the Son being honored in a God-befitting manner; he who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him, for He does not accept honor upon the dishonor of a Son. For He sent me through the flesh, not that I might be insulted, but that I might be glorified (John 12:28).

Therefore, because you have turned against me ignorantly, for this reason and through this flesh which was sent to Him, I said: Father, glorify your Son (John 12:28). You, glorify the one whom these insult; You also glorify the flesh being set aside by them, so that they may know that you will glorify even the man from Mary without distinction as a Father, through the fellowship toward your only-begotten Son, giving glory now to the temple taken up by me, which I myself had with you by nature before the ages...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
